metadata.name: Classic Maya Core Dictionary
metadata.description: Core vocabulary of Classic Maya (Ch'olti'an) compiled from epigraphic sources

titles_and_ranks.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *ajaw; widespread across all Classic Maya inscriptions
Compound of k'uhul (sacred/divine) + ajaw (lord); first attested in early Classic period
Possibly from *kalom 'tree' + te' 'wood/tree'; exact etymology debated (Stuart 2000)
Compound: b'aah (head/first) + kab' (earth/land); honorific indicating primacy within a polity
Derivation uncertain; title of secondary lords subordinate to an ajaw
Compound: y-ajaw (his lord) + k'ahk' (fire); military title, possibly commander of fire-drill warfare rituals
Proto-Ch'olano *ch'ok 'youth, sprout'; metaphor of plant sprout for heir
Proto-Mayan *ix 'woman, female'; gender marker prefixed to names and titles
Derived from ix (woman) + -ik nominal suffix; denotes noble or royal women
Compound: b'aah (head/first) + kab' (earth/land); variant of b'aah kab', used interchangeably
ti' (at/mouth) + sak (white) + huun (paper/headband); refers to the white paper headband worn by heirs apparent
ah (agent prefix) + k'in (sun/day); literally 'he of the sun/day', priestly title
From itz' (resin, precious thing) + -aat suffix; one who deals in precious/sacred knowledge
Compound: k'in (sun) + ich (eye/face); 'sun-eyed' or 'radiant'; prefixed to royal names to denote solar divinity
Compound: ix (female prefix) + kaloomte' (supreme lord); highest female military-political title in Classic Maya epigraphy
usage_examples: Ix Kaloomte' Yohl Ik'nal of Palenque

titles_and_ranks.etymology: Compound: y-ajaw (his lord) + te' (tree/wood); title of a subordinate lord, possibly a forest or regional governor
Compound: aj (agent prefix) + tz'ihb' (to write/paint); 'he who writes'; title for royal scribes and painters
usage_examples: aj tz'ihb' title in Copán hieroglyphic stairway

titles_and_ranks.spanish: sacerdote del sol, guardián del calendario
titles_and_ranks.etymology: Compound: aj (agent prefix) + k'in (sun/day); 'he of the sun/day'; priestly title for calendar specialists
usage_examples: aj k'in in calendrical ritual contexts

titles_and_ranks.etymology: Compound: ux (three) + yop (leaf) + huun (headband/paper); the three-leaf headband worn by rulers in Period Ending contexts
usage_examples: ux yop huun in accession imagery

titles_and_ranks.etymology: Compound: k'ahk' (fire) + ti' (mouth) + ch'ok (youth); epithet for royal heirs engaged in warfare or fire rituals
usage_examples: k'ahk' ti' ch'ok in warrior prince contexts

verbs.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *chum 'to sit'; accession verb meaning 'seated in rulership'
Proto-Ch'olano *hul 'to arrive'; frequently records arrivals of rulers or deities
Proto-Ch'olano *och 'to enter'; used in death phrases (och b'ih, och ha') and accession contexts
Proto-Ch'olano *tz'ihb' 'to paint, write'; the scribal act
Proto-Ch'olano *ch'ak 'to chop, cut'; the primary Classic Maya warfare verb, depicting axe attacks
Proto-Ch'olano *hub' 'to topple, fall'; warfare/destruction verb
Root jub' 'to descend, fall'; used for descent of celestial objects and in defeat expressions
Proto-Mayan *il 'to see'; one of the most basic verbs in Maya
Related to nak 'belly, layer'; meaning 'to layer/stack stones'; used in construction dedications
Proto-Ch'olano *k'al 'to tie, bind'; used for Period Ending rituals (k'al tun = tying of the stone)
Proto-Ch'olano *tzak 'to summon, conjure'; the primary verb for ritual invocation of supernatural beings
Proto-Ch'olano *pat 'to form, make'; used in creation contexts and dedicatory phrases
Proto-Ch'olano *lok' 'to exit, emerge'; antonym of och; used for emergence events
Proto-Ch'olano *cham 'to die'; the primary death verb in Classic inscriptions
Proto-Ch'olano *siy 'to be born'; primary birth verb in Classic inscriptions
Proto-Ch'olano *jatz' 'to beat, hit'; warfare and punishment verb
Proto-Ch'olano *pul 'to burn'; used in incense-offering and auto-sacrifice contexts
Possibly related to k'ux 'heart/gnaw'; eating verb, appears in offering contexts
Proto-Ch'olano *uk' 'to drink'; used in vessel dedications and ritual drinking
Related to pas 'dawn, open'; used in portal and ritual opening contexts
Proto-Ch'olano *k'am 'to receive, accept'; used for receiving titles, captives, or tribute
Proto-Ch'olano *pak' 'to plant'; used in agricultural and metaphorical contexts for founding or establishing
Proto-Ch'olano *tz'ap 'to plant, set upright'; the primary verb for erecting stelae and monuments

verbs.english: it happened, it came to pass
verbs.etymology: Perfective aspect of ti 'to happen, occur'; stock phrase introducing historical events in narrative texts
usage_examples: u-ti-ya ta k'atun (it happened at the k'atun)

verbs.etymology: Ergative perfective of il 'to see'; y-il (he-saw); witnessing events is a key royal prerogative recorded in inscriptions
Proto-Ch'olano *b'aj 'to hit, hammer'; used in warfare and in bloodletting rites where a bone awl is used
Related to wol 'round, assembled'; used for gatherings of tribute, people, or ritual participants
Proto-Ch'olano *joy 'to encircle, go around'; used for ritual circumambulation of monuments and territories
Proto-Ch'olano *em 'to descend'; used for descent of rulers to the underworld, descent of celestial bodies, and political submission
Possibly related to let 'to accompany, serve'; used for subordinate service to a lord or deity
Proto-Mayan *pik 'eight thousand'; the vigesimal unit of 8,000; used in counting tribute and large quantities
Verb phrase: k'al (to bind) + tuun (stone); the ritual act of binding/completing a stone at Period Ending ceremonies
Possibly homophonous with nah 'house'; verbal form meaning 'to adorn/anoint' or 'to dream/envision', used in auto-sacrifice contexts

nouns.etymology: Proto-Mayan *q'ij 'sun, day'; fundamental calendrical and cosmological term
Proto-Mayan *ja' 'water'; fundamental element, used in place names and death expressions
Proto-Ch'olano *witz 'mountain'; represents the Maya cosmos as a mountain, used in site names
Proto-Ch'olano *nah 'house'; used in building dedications and cosmic house metaphors
Derived from k'uh (god/spirit) + -ul adjectival suffix; divine quality
Proto-Ch'olano *k'uh 'god, spirit, sacred'; root of k'uhul
Proto-Ch'olano *b'aah 'head, first, self, image'; polysemous term central to royal identity
Proto-Ch'olano *b'ahlam 'jaguar'; the most prestigious animal in Maya culture, used in royal names
Proto-Ch'olano *way 'sleep, dream, spirit companion'; the animal alter-ego of rulers and deities
Proto-Ch'olano *k'ahk' 'fire'; used in names, military titles, and ritual contexts
Proto-Mayan *saq 'white'; color of the north in Maya directional symbolism
Proto-Mayan *ek' 'black, star' (note: same root for black and star in many Mayan languages); also means 'black'
Proto-Ch'olano *tun 'stone'; also the 360-day period in the Long Count; k'al tun = Period Ending
Proto-Ch'olano *nal 'corn, place'; fundamental crop and suffix meaning 'place of X'
Proto-Mayan *iq' 'wind, breath, spirit'; life force and one of the 20 day names
Proto-Ch'olano *ak'b'al 'night, darkness'; day name and underworld concept
Proto-Mayan *kab' 'earth, honey'; polysemous; earth as cosmic surface and honey as sacred substance
Proto-Ch'olano *chan 'sky, four, serpent'; polysemous term; also the Kaan dynasty emblem
Proto-Ch'olano *pakal 'shield'; used in personal names (K'inich Janaab Pakal) and military contexts
Proto-Ch'olano *tok' 'flint, obsidian'; paired with pakal (flint and shield) as warfare symbol
Possibly related to Proto-Ch'olano *muyal 'cloud'; used in celestial and supernatural contexts
Variant spelling of tun; Proto-Ch'olano *tun 'stone'; used in monument and dedication contexts
Proto-Ch'olano *lak 'plate, companion'; vessel term found in pottery dedication texts
Proto-Mayan *te' 'tree, wood'; used as a classifier and in compound terms (kaloomte')
Related to Proto-Ch'olano *chit 'father'; kinship term used in genealogical statements
Proto-Mayan *na' 'mother'; kinship term used in matrilineal descent phrases
Alternative term for jaguar; possibly related to a specific color-phase or species variant
Proto-Ch'olano *ajiin 'crocodile'; the Cosmic Crocodile represents the earth's surface in Maya cosmology
Compound: sak (white) + huun (paper/headband); the white paper headband is the primary marker of royal heirs and rulers
usage_examples: ti' sak huun (bearer of the white headband)

nouns.spanish: dios del rayo y la abundancia
nouns.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *k'awiil 'lightning deity'; God K in the Schellhas classification; the manikin scepter wielded by rulers
Proto-Ch'olano *naah 'first, primary'; used as an ordinal prefix and in compound titles; distinct from nah 'house' in some analyses
Proto-Ch'olano *sib'ik 'soot, black smoke'; copal incense smoke is the breath of the gods; soot marks ritual fire events
Possibly related to Proto-Ch'olano *b'uj 'vessel'; used for ritual drinking and cacao containers
Proto-Ch'olano *tz'ib' 'writing, painting'; the noun form of tz'ihb'; the script itself and individual glyphs
Variant of b'ahlam; Proto-Ch'olano *b'alam 'jaguar'; used in Yucatecan and some Ch'olan texts
Proto-Ch'olano *kooj 'mask'; ritual masks are used in deity impersonation ceremonies; the mask transforms the wearer into a divine being
Compound: lakam (large, banner) + tun (stone); the standard term for a carved stone monument (stela)
usage_examples: hub'uy u lakam tun (the stela was toppled)

nouns.etymology: Proto-Mayan *hun 'paper, one'; paper is sacred — made from fig bark and used for codices and royal headbands
Compound: k'an (yellow/precious) + tok (flint/obsidian); precious stone blades used in bloodletting and sacrifice
Proto-Ch'olano *ak'b'al 'night, darkness'; used in creation phrases (ch'ab' ak'ab') and underworld contexts
Plural of way 'spirit companion'; wayob' are the collective supernatural familiars of the ruling class depicted on way ceramics
Proto-Mayan *ixiim 'maize grain'; Juun Ixiim (One Maize) is the name of the Maize God in some texts
Compound: chak (red/great) + chuen (monkey artisan, day sign); patron deity of scribes and craftsmen
Proto-Mayan *eb' 'stair, step'; pyramid stairs are the axis mundi; also a day name in the Tzolk'in calendar
Proto-Ch'olano *patan 'tribute, service rendered to a lord'; records of tribute payment appear in subordinate polity texts
Proto-Mayan *nik 'flower'; flowers are offerings to deities and symbols of beauty, blood, and the sun
Derived from ajaw (lord) + -lel abstract suffix; 'the condition of being lord'; the abstract concept of royal authority

adjectives_and_colors.etymology: Proto-Mayan *yax 'green/blue, new, first'; color of vegetation, water, and the east in some traditions
Proto-Mayan *saq 'white'; color of the north, bone, and purity; used in titles and place names
Proto-Mayan *ek' 'black'; color of the west in directional symbolism; also means 'star' in some contexts
Proto-Mayan *chak 'red, large, great'; color of the east; also the Rain God's name
Proto-Mayan *q'an 'yellow, ripe, precious'; color of the south; also means 'ripe corn'
Possibly from Proto-Ch'olano *nuk 'large, great'; intensifier for size and importance
Proto-Mayan *waq 'six'; also means 'upright, erected' in compound words; Wakah Chan = erected sky (World Tree)
usage_examples: Wakah Chan Te' (World Tree — erected sky tree)

adjectives_and_colors.etymology: Derived from k'uh (god) + -ul adjectival suffix; 'of divine essence'; the most important royal epithet
Proto-Ch'olano *lakam 'large, banner'; quality adjective for large size or importance; also 'banner/standard'
Yucatec Mayan *noh 'large, great, important'; used in Yucatecan and some lowland contexts as size/importance marker
usage_examples: Noh Mul (great mound, Belizean site name)

adjectives_and_colors.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *tz'ak 'in order, succession'; used in dynastic succession statements and ordered sequences

directional_terms.etymology: Compound: lak'in from Proto-Ch'olano *lak'in 'east'; associated with sunrise, red, and birth
Proto-Ch'olano *chik'in 'west'; associated with sunset, black, and death
Proto-Ch'olano *xaman 'north'; associated with white, cold, ancestors, and the Milky Way
Proto-Ch'olano *nohol 'south'; associated with yellow, warmth, and the underworld in some traditions
Proto-Mayan *yok 'above, on top'; the vertical axis; used in cosmological texts for celestial positions
Proto-Mayan *ti' 'at, toward, mouth'; the primary locative/directional preposition in Classic Maya
Possibly related to naah 'first/house'; in some contexts used directionally for 'deep within' or 'below'

numerals.etymology: Proto-Mayan *b'olon 'nine'; sacred number of the underworld
Compound: ux (3) + lajun (10); 13 is the sacred number of the upper world
Compound: waxak (8) + lajun (10); 18 = number of months in Haab'
Compound: b'olon (9) + lajun (10); 19 = maximum in vigesimal position

death_expressions.etymology: Compound: och (to enter) + b'ih (road/path); the road metaphor for death is widespread in Maya texts
Compound: och (to enter) + ha' (water); entering the underworld waters
k'a'ay (was extinguished/lost) + u (his/her) + sak (white) + ik'il (breath/wind essence); poetic death expression
Proto-Ch'olano *cham 'to die'; as a noun 'the death'; appears in mortuary contexts and Death God names
Verb phrase: och (enter) + ta (at/into) + b'ih (road); the road of death; a more elaborate form of och b'ih
usage_examples: och ta b'ih-iiy (he entered the road)

death_expressions.etymology: Compound: sak (white) + b'aak (bone) + naah (house); a euphemism for the tomb or funerary chamber in some texts
Intransitive verb from k'ay 'to be lost, extinguished'; used specifically in death contexts for the extinguishing of the breath-soul
usage_examples: k'a'ay u sak ik'il (white breath was extinguished)

war_expressions.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *ch'ak 'to chop'; the primary Classic warfare verb; depicted by axe-wielding figures
Passive of hub' 'to topple'; records the destruction of a polity or defeat of a ruler

war_expressions.notes: Venus warfare glyph, associated with planetary cycles
war_expressions.etymology: Glyph complex combining star/Venus glyph over a defeated site; linked to Venus superior conjunctions

war_expressions.spanish: fue derribado su pedernal y escudo
war_expressions.english: his flint and shield were cast down (defeated)
war_expressions.etymology: jub'uy (was cast down, passive) + u tok' pakal (his flint and shield); stock phrase for defeat
usage_examples: defeat of a ruler recorded at Dos Pilas

war_expressions.etymology: Proto-Mayan *b'aak 'bone, captive'; captives are named with b'ak prefix in captive-taking texts
Compound: chak (red/great) + chij (deer); metaphor for a sacrificed captive as a hunted deer; the ruler as hunter
Compound: och k'in (west = sunset direction) + kaloomte' (supreme lord); directional military title claimed by powerful rulers
Proto-Ch'olano *tok' 'flint blade'; bloodletting and sacrificial instrument; paired with pakal (shield) as war symbol
Compound: ek' (black/night) + ch'ak (axe event); proposed compound for nocturnal surprise attacks
usage_examples: possible night raid context at Naranjo

kinship.etymology: Proto-Mayan *mam 'grandfather, ancestor'; refers to venerated forebears and dynastic lineage heads
Proto-Mayan *na' 'mother'; matrilineal kinship term used in genealogical texts and birth records
Proto-Mayan *yum 'father, lord'; paternal kinship term used in genealogical and honorific contexts
Proto-Ch'olano *atan 'wife'; used in marriage statements and dynastic alliances
Proto-Ch'olano *nich'an 'son of father'; patrilineal descent term in royal genealogies
Proto-Mayan *yal 'child of mother'; matrilineal descent marker used in birth and succession statements
Proto-Ch'olano *yitzihn 'younger sibling/brother'; recorded in succession disputes and co-ruler texts
Proto-Ch'olano *sakuun 'elder brother'; seniority term in dynastic succession texts
Proto-Ch'olano *mihin 'child, offspring'; general offspring term used in both genders
Proto-Mayan *ix 'woman, female'; gender marker prefixed to women's names, titles, and kinship terms
Proto-Mayan *winik 'person, man, twenty'; polysemous — also the vigesimal unit of 20
Proto-Ch'olano *ch'ok 'youth, sprout'; metaphor of plant sprout for the royal heir
Possessed form: y- (his) + atan (wife); used in dynastic marriage alliance texts and genealogical statements
Possessed form: y- (his/her) + alaw (grandchild); grandchildren are named in dynastic legitimization texts
Compound: ajaw (lord) + na' (mother); the queen mother title for a woman who is mother of the reigning lord
Variant of sakuun; Proto-Ch'olano *sukuun 'elder brother'; used in succession and co-rulership texts
Proto-Ch'olano *ch'ab' 'creation, penance, bloodline'; the lineage created through bloodletting penance
Derived from b'aah (head/first/image) + -il nominal suffix; the image or portrait of a ruler, also 'the foremost person'
Compound: ix (female) + tab (rope, cord); the goddess associated with the noose and suicide by hanging; a merciful death deity

architecture.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *nah 'house'; the basic term for a constructed dwelling or ritual structure
Proto-Ch'olano *otoot 'home, abode'; connotes permanent residence as distinct from a temporary structure
Compound: pib' (underground oven/heat) + naah (house); the ritual sweat bath used for purification
Derived from way (sleep/spirit) + -ib' instrumental suffix; place where spirit companions dwell
Compound: k'uhul (sacred/divine) + nah (house); the standard term for a temple or shrine
Possessed form of otoot: y- (his/her) + otoot (home); the royal palace as the ruler's home
Proto-Ch'olano *witz 'mountain'; pyramidal temples conceived as sacred mountains in Maya cosmology
Proto-Ch'olano *hol 'hole, opening, head'; used for doorways and cave entrances as portals to the supernatural
Proto-Mayan *peten 'island, enclosed land'; used for the Petén lowlands region and island settlements
Compound: sak (white) + nah (house); white stucco structures associated with dawn, purity, and cosmic renewal
Proto-Mayan *b'ih 'road, path'; the white causeways (sacbeob) connecting ceremonial centers
Compound: lakam (large, banner) + ha' (water); the ancient name of Palenque referring to the Usumacinta watershed
Proto-Ch'olano *tzak 'to conjure, summon, build'; used both for architectural construction and ritual invocation
Compound: ek' (black) + huun (paper/headband); the black headband worn by scribes and certain ritual specialists
Compound: kaloomte' (supreme warrior title) + nah (house); hypothetical compound for elite warrior structures
Compound: ak'ab' (night/darkness) + nah (house); the night house is the western celestial house of the Sun God's nightly passage
usage_examples: ak'ab' nah in cosmological house texts
night house at Palenque cross group

architecture.etymology: Compound: chan (sky) + nah (house); the celestial house at the apex of the cosmic mountain; one of the four cosmological houses
usage_examples: chan nah in Palenque tablet cosmology

architecture.etymology: Compound: k'in (sun) + nah (house); the eastern solar house; the Temple of the Sun at Palenque is the k'in nah
usage_examples: k'in nah = Temple of the Sun at Palenque

architecture.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *lakam 'large, banner'; used in lakamha' (Palenque) and lakam tun (stela); banners mark royal and ritual spaces

flora_fauna.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *b'ahlam 'jaguar'; the most prestigious animal in Maya culture, symbol of kingship and the night sun
Proto-Ch'olano *mo' 'macaw'; the scarlet macaw is the solar bird in Maya iconography
Proto-Ch'olano *muwan 'hawk, owl'; raptor bird associated with war and the underworld
Proto-Mayan *k'uk' 'quetzal'; the quetzal feather is the supreme symbol of royal beauty and power
Proto-Mayan *tz'ikin 'bird'; generic bird term and one of the 20 Maya day names
usage_examples: Yaxuun B'ahlam (Yaxchilan ruler name with bird)

flora_fauna.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *chan/*kaan 'serpent, sky'; the Vision Serpent is the primary conduit to the supernatural world
Alternative or dialectal term for jaguar/ocelot; may indicate a specific spotted feline species
Proto-Mayan *chij 'deer'; deer hunting was a ritual and elite activity; deer featured in creation narratives
Proto-Ch'olano *ahiin 'crocodile'; the Cosmic Crocodile (Itzam Kab' Ahiin) represents the earth's surface
Derived from way (spirit companion) + -is nominal suffix; the supernatural animal alter-ego of rulers
Proto-Mayan *kakaw 'cacao'; the sacred drink of rulers; chocolate beverages appear in vessel dedication texts
Proto-Ch'olano *nal 'corn, place of'; the Maize God (Hun Hunahpu/Juun Ixiim) is central to Maya creation mythology
Proto-Mayan *che' 'tree, wood'; the World Tree (Wakah Chan Te') is the cosmic axis mundi
Proto-Mayan *ja' 'water'; fundamental to Maya agriculture, cosmology, and the underworld
Possibly related to ik' (wind/dark) + at suffix; toads associated with rain, fertility, and the underworld
Proto-Mayan *b'atz' 'howler monkey'; the monkey scribes (Hun B'atz' and Hun Chowen) are patron deities of scribes and artists
usage_examples: b'atz' day sign in Tzolk'in calendar

flora_fauna.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *koj 'puma, lion'; the puma is a secondary feline power symbol used in warrior titles
Proto-Ch'olano *tz'unuum 'hummingbird'; the hummingbird is a royal and solar bird, associated with flower rituals
Proto-Mayan *ch'o' 'mouse, rat'; rodents appear in underworld contexts and as way spirit companions
Proto-Mayan *pek' 'dog'; dogs guide the dead through the underworld and appear in funerary contexts
Compound: yax (first/green) + te' (tree); the ceiba (Ceiba pentandra) is the World Tree (axis mundi) in Maya cosmology
usage_examples: Wakah Chan Yax Te' (World Tree name)

flora_fauna.etymology: Proto-Mayan *kab' 'bee, honey, earth'; honey is a sacred offering; the same root gives 'earth' in many Mayan languages

astronomy.etymology: Proto-Mayan *q'ij 'sun, day'; the sun is both timekeeper and deity (K'inich Ajaw, the Sun God)
Proto-Mayan *uh 'moon'; the Moon Goddess (Ix Uh) governs the lunar calendar and fertility
Proto-Mayan *ek' 'black, star'; the same root yields both color and celestial referent across Mayan languages
Proto-Ch'olano *k'ahk' 'fire'; fire is central to Period Ending rituals and astronomical new-fire ceremonies
Proto-Mayan *iq' 'wind, breath, spirit'; one of the 20 day names; Ik' Sijom (Wind God) in creation texts
Possibly from Proto-Ch'olano *muyal 'cloud'; clouds are the breath of mountains and associated with rain deities
Proto-Ch'olano *chaahk 'rain deity'; the paramount weather god who wields a stone axe to create thunder and lightning
Compound: k'in (sun) + ich (eye/face); 'sun-eyed' epithet of the Sun God and solar rulers

astronomy.spanish: Venus como estrella de la mañana
astronomy.etymology: Compound: yax (first/green) + ek' (star); the first star of morning = Venus as morning star (heliacal rising)
Compound: chak (great/red) + ek' (star); the great red star = Venus as evening star (superior conjunction)
Proto-Ch'olano *way 'sleep, dream, spirit companion'; dream visions were the channel for astronomical omens
From xib' 'fear' + -alb'a locative suffix; the place of fright/trembling — the nine-level underworld
usage_examples: Xibalba lords in Popol Vuh context

astronomy.etymology: Compound: sak (white) + ik' (wind/breath); the life-force wind associated with the north direction and dawn
usage_examples: k'a'ay u sak ik'il (white breath expired = death)

astronomy.etymology: Compound: b'olon (nine) + tz'akab' (generation/succession); epithet meaning 'of nine generations' applied to deities and nobles
Compound: lahun (ten) + chan (sky); the tenth celestial level in Maya layered cosmos; appears in astronomical and supernatural contexts
usage_examples: lahun chan in thirteen-sky cosmological scheme

astronomy.etymology: Proto-Mayan *waxaq 'eight'; used in calendar dates and the name Waxaklajun Ub'aah Kaan (Snake kingdom ruler)
Orthographic variant of chaahk; Proto-Ch'olano *chaahk 'rain deity'; the storm god who sends lightning and controls rain
Possibly from itz' (resin/precious) + am (spider) + naaj (great); the supreme deity and lord of the heavens
Compound: ox (three) + lahun (ten) = thirteen; 13 is the number of upper sky levels in Maya cosmology

rituals.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *ch'am 'to receive, grasp'; used for receiving scepters, captives, and ritual objects
Proto-Ch'olano *k'al 'to tie, bind'; the Period Ending ritual (k'al tun) marks calendrical milestones
Proto-Ch'olano *chok 'to scatter, throw'; the scattering of copal incense is depicted on numerous stelae
Root jub' 'to descend, fall'; used for descent of deities, celestial bodies, and in defeat expressions
Proto-Ch'olano *tzak 'to summon, conjure'; primary verb for calling forth supernatural beings through blood ritual
Proto-Ch'olano *k'uh 'god, spirit, sacred essence'; the animating sacred force in all ritual objects and places
Proto-Ch'olano *pib' 'underground oven'; used in the pib'naah (sweat bath) and ritual cooking of offerings
Proto-Ch'olano *way 'sleep, dream, spirit companion'; the animal alter-ego summoned in shamanic rituals
Proto-Ch'olano *ohl 'heart, center, desire'; the spiritual and physical center of being; heart extraction in sacrifice
usage_examples: u ohl ajaw (heart of the lord)

rituals.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *b'aah 'head, first, self'; the head is the locus of identity in auto-sacrifice and portrait rituals
Proto-Ch'olano *tz'ihb' 'to paint, write'; the scribal act is itself ritualized; scribes are divine intermediaries
Proto-Ch'olano *ak'ot 'to dance'; ritual dance is a form of divine impersonation and calendrical performance
Proto-Ch'olano *ch'ab' 'creation, penance'; used in the creation compound ch'ab' ak'ab' (creation and darkness)
Proto-Ch'olano *pax 'to play music, drum'; music is integral to ceremonial gatherings and ritual calendar events
Proto-Ch'olano *lok' 'to exit, emerge'; the antonym of och (enter); used for emergence of deities from portals
Proto-Ch'olano *jatz' 'to beat, hit'; ritual striking of captives and ball-game sacrifice
Proto-Ch'olano *wak' 'to rise, raise'; used for raising standards, stelae, and the erection of ritual objects
usage_examples: lifting of the World Tree ritual

rituals.etymology: Related to k'as 'knot, bind'; binding rites including captive binding and ritual cord-tying at Period Endings
Related to b'ol 'predator, to prey upon'; a powerful beast associated with elite warriors and military raids
Possibly related to ko- verbal prefix + kan 'offer'; presentation of tribute, gifts, or sacrificial offerings to a superior
Proto-Ch'olano *mak 'to cover, seal'; used for sealing tombs, closing ritual spaces, and covering monuments
Proto-Mayan *yax 'green/blue, first, new'; when used in ritual contexts it marks inaugurals and new beginnings
usage_examples: yax ch'am ajawlel (first reception of lordship)

rituals.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *pul 'to burn'; incense burning is the standard offering to supernatural beings

toponyms.etymology: Compound: lakam (large/banner) + ha' (water); the ancient name of the Palenque site, referring to its abundant rivers
From *mutal 'bundle, tied together'; the emblem glyph of Tikal, one of the largest Classic Maya cities
Compound: ux (three) + witz (mountain) + a' (water); 'three mountain water'; the ancient name of Copán
From *pa'chan 'split sky'; the ancient name of the Yaxchilán site on the Usumacinta River
From *kaan 'serpent/sky'; the Kaan (Snake) Kingdom, centered at Calakmul, was the dominant Classic Maya superpower
From *sa'al 'gruel place' or 'watery place'; the ancient name of the Naranjo site in the Petén
Compound: hux (three) + witz (mountain) + a' (water); variant name, possibly for Caracol, Belize
From *b'aakal 'bone'; the dynastic kingdom name of Palenque; the B'aakal (Bone) kingdom emblem glyph
usage_examples: K'uhul B'aakal Ajaw (holy lord of Palenque)

toponyms.etymology: From *waka' 'standing water' or topographic term; ancient name of the site now called El Perú in Petén, Guatemala
From *yokib' 'at the entrance/port'; the ancient name of Piedras Negras on the Usumacinta River
Compound: kan (four/serpent) + witz (mountain) + nal (place of); 'place of the four-snake mountain'; the dynastic name of Quiriguá
Compound: k'an (yellow/precious) + witz (mountain); topographic site name element used in several polity names
usage_examples: k'an witz in site emblem glyphs

toponyms.etymology: Compound: sak (white) + nikte' (plumeria flower); white plumeria appears in site names and as a feminine beauty epithet
Compound: ox (three) + te' (tree/word) + tuun (stone); the three hearthstones of creation set at the beginning of the current era
usage_examples: ox te' tuun in creation narrative

body_parts.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *b'aah 'head, first, self, image'; polysemous and central to Maya identity; u b'aah = himself
Proto-Mayan *chi' 'mouth'; used in speech act glyphs, dedicatory phrases, and portal imagery
Proto-Mayan *ich 'eye, face, inside'; k'inich = sun-eye; used in K'inich (Sun God) epithets
Proto-Ch'olano *jol 'skull, head'; used in death imagery and as a day name variant
usage_examples: jol skull imagery in death expressions

body_parts.etymology: Proto-Mayan *k'ab' 'hand, arm, branch'; the hand as instrument of action, writing, and bloodletting
Proto-Mayan *ook 'foot'; footprint glyphs record arrivals, pilgrimages, and territorial claims
Proto-Mayan *ti' 'mouth, at, edge'; used as a preposition (at/to) and as a body part (mouth/lip)
usage_examples: ti' sak huun (mouth of the white headband)

body_parts.etymology: Proto-Ch'olano *nak 'belly, interior, layer'; used in construction contexts (to layer/stack) and body references
Proto-Ch'olano *ohl 'heart, center, will'; the heart is both physical and spiritual; heart sacrifice is the supreme offering
Proto-Mayan *b'aak 'bone, captive'; homophonous with b'aak 'captive' — bones of sacrificed captives were kept as trophies
Proto-Ch'olano *tzutz 'hair'; royal hair is shorn at captive-taking and sacrificed; hair offerings appear in ritual texts
Proto-Mayan *ni' 'nose, tip, point'; the nose is a site for bloodletting by perforation in auto-sacrifice rituals
Proto-Ch'olano *lem 'mirror, shine'; pyrite and obsidian mirrors are portals to the supernatural and markers of divinity
Possessed form: u (his/her) + b'aah (head/self/image); 'his/her image' — the standard way to say 'himself' or a portrait in Classic Maya
usage_examples: u b'aah k'awiil (the image of K'awiil)

time_periods.etymology: Proto-Mayan *q'ij 'sun, day'; the base unit of the Long Count calendar; also the Solar face glyph
From winik 'person, 20'; the vigesimal unit of 20 days; also called uinal in older literature
Proto-Ch'olano *tun 'stone, 360-day period'; the tun is the base of Period Ending ceremonies (k'al tun)
usage_examples: k'al tun (tying the stone = Period Ending)

time_periods.etymology: Compound: k' (prefix) + tun (360-day period) × 20 = 7,200 days; the primary dynastic time unit
Compound: b'ak' (400) × tun; 144,000 days = approximately 394 solar years; the largest Long Count unit in common use
Proto-Mayan *hab' 'year, season'; the 365-day vague solar year (18 months of 20 days + 5-day Wayeb')
Ch'olan term for the b'ak'tun; pih means 'bundle of 400'; related to the Aztec concept of xihuitl bundles
Compound: winik (20) + haab' (year); the 20-year cycle also called k'atun; used in later Postclassic texts
usage_examples: winikhaab' as k'atun equivalent in Ch'olan texts

time_periods.spanish: atadura de la piedra (fin de período)
time_periods.etymology: Compound: k'al (to bind) + tuun (stone); the ritual binding of the stone at Period Endings marks calendrical transitions
Compound: lahun (10) + tun (360-day period); the mid-k'atun Period Ending, marking 3,600 days
Compound: ho' (five) + tuun (360-day period); 1,800-day quarter of the k'atun; marks intermediate Period Ending ceremonies
Compound: ox (three) + lajun (ten) = thirteen; the sacred number of heavenly levels; 13 day-names cycle in the Tzolk'in
Proto-Mayan *b'olon 'nine'; the number of underworld levels and the Bolon Ti' K'uh (nine deities); a sacred count
Compound: laj (ten) + cha' (two) = twelve; used in Long Count dates and in the names of twelve-night ritual cycles
usage_examples: lajchan in Long Count date contexts

time_periods.etymology: Modern K'iche' scholarly term; Classic Maya called it simply the 'count of days'; 13 numbers × 20 day names = 260 days

time_periods.spanish: señor del sol, fecha de fin de período
time_periods.english: lord of the sun, Period Ending date
time_periods.etymology: Compound: ajaw (lord) + k'in (sun/day); the 'lord sun' day name that falls at Period Endings in the Calendar Round
